subject: computing
subtitle: Using IF, ELIF, and ELSE statements to control program flow based on conditions.

data.targetWord: A programming construct that chooses between different execution paths based on whether a condition evaluates to true or false

examples.en-GB: Selection allows a program to output 'Pass' or 'Fail' depending on whether the score is above 50.

data.targetWord: An expression used in a selection statement that evaluates to either True or False

examples.en-GB: The condition score >= 50 evaluates to True if score is 50 or above, and False otherwise.

data.targetWord: A selection statement that executes a block of code only when its condition is True; if the condition is False, the block is skipped

examples.en-GB: IF score >= 50 THEN OUTPUT "You passed!" ENDIF — this only prints the message when the condition is True.

data.targetWord: The block of code in a selection statement that executes when none of the preceding IF or ELIF conditions are True

examples.en-GB: The ELSE block runs when the IF condition is False, providing an alternative outcome for the program.

data.targetWord: Short for 'else if' — an additional condition checked only when all preceding IF and ELIF conditions were False

examples.en-GB: ELIF temperature > 15 THEN OUTPUT "Warm" — this line is only reached if the previous IF condition was False.

data.targetWord: An operator that compares two values and returns a Boolean result of True or False; examples include ==, !=, <, >, <=, >=

examples.en-GB: The comparison operator >= returns True if the left value is greater than or equal to the right value.

data.targetWord: An operator that combines Boolean values or expressions; the three logical operators are AND, OR, and NOT

examples.en-GB: Using a logical operator such as AND allows two conditions to be combined: score >= 50 AND score < 75.

data.targetWord: A logical operator that returns True only when both of its operand conditions are True; if either is False, the result is False

examples.en-GB: age >= 18 AND hasTicket == True is True only when both conditions hold at the same time.

data.targetWord: A logical operator that returns True when at least one of its operand conditions is True; it is only False when both are False

examples.en-GB: colour == "red" OR colour == "amber" is True when either colour is red or colour is amber.

data.targetWord: A logical operator that inverts a Boolean value: NOT True becomes False, and NOT False becomes True

examples.en-GB: IF NOT isLoggedIn THEN OUTPUT "Please log in." — the block runs only when isLoggedIn is False.

data.targetWord: An IF statement placed inside another IF statement, allowing more complex decision-making with multiple levels of conditions

examples.en-GB: A nested IF can first check whether a user is old enough, then inside that block check whether they have a ticket.

data.targetWord: An expression that evaluates to either True or False; used as the condition in IF statements and WHILE loops

examples.en-GB: score >= 50 AND score < 75 is a Boolean expression that is True only when the score is in the Merit range.

data.targetWord: Spaces at the start of a line used in Python to define which statements belong to a particular block; indentation is mandatory and errors will cause a program to fail

examples.en-GB: In Python, the four spaces before print("You passed!") tell the interpreter that this line is inside the IF block.

data.targetWord: One of the possible execution paths in a selection statement; each IF, ELIF, or ELSE creates a separate branch

examples.en-GB: An IF-ELIF-ELSE structure with four options creates four branches, but only one branch executes for any given input.

data.targetWord: One of the two Boolean values; a condition is true when it correctly describes the current state of the program's data

examples.en-GB: The condition 10 > 5 is true because ten is indeed greater than five.

data.targetWord: One of the two Boolean values; a condition is false when it does not correctly describe the current state of the program's data

examples.en-GB: The condition 3 > 10 is false because three is not greater than ten.

data.targetWord: The comparison operator that tests whether two values are equal and returns True if they are, False if they are not

examples.en-GB: password == "secret" returns True only if the variable password holds exactly the string "secret".

data.targetWord: The operator in Python that stores a value into a variable; it is not a comparison and must not be used inside an IF condition

examples.en-GB: score = 85 uses the assignment operator to store the value 85 in the variable score.

data.targetWord: The comparison operator < that returns True when the left value is smaller than the right value

examples.en-GB: age < 18 returns True when age is 17 or below, and False when age is 18 or above.

data.targetWord: The comparison operator > that returns True when the left value is larger than the right value

examples.en-GB: score > 100 returns True only when score exceeds 100.

data.targetWord: The comparison operator <= that returns True when the left value is smaller than or exactly equal to the right value

examples.en-GB: temperature <= 0 returns True for temperatures of 0 degrees and below, including negative values.

data.targetWord: The comparison operator >= that returns True when the left value is larger than or exactly equal to the right value

examples.en-GB: score >= 50 returns True for scores of exactly 50 as well as all scores above 50.

data.targetWord: The comparison operator != that returns True when the two values being compared are different

examples.en-GB: password != "correct" returns True when the user's password does not match, so the program knows to reject the attempt.

data.targetWord: A group of statements that belong together and are executed as a unit, defined by indentation in Python

examples.en-GB: All statements indented under an IF line form a block; they all execute together when the condition is True.

data.targetWord: The mechanisms that determine the order in which instructions are executed, including sequence, selection, and iteration

examples.en-GB: Selection is one form of flow control: it directs the program to execute different blocks based on conditions.

data.targetWord: A point in a program where the execution path splits based on a condition; represented as a diamond shape in a flowchart

examples.en-GB: The question 'Is score >= 50?' is a decision point: depending on the answer, the program takes one of two paths.

data.targetWord: A selection construct that matches a variable against a list of specific values and executes the matching block; an alternative to long IF-ELIF chains

examples.en-GB: A CASE statement can match a day number (1–7) to a day name more clearly than seven separate ELIF conditions.

data.targetWord: A data type with exactly two possible values, True or False; used as the result of conditions in selection and iteration

examples.en-GB: Every condition in an IF statement produces a Boolean result: it is either True (run the block) or False (skip it).

data.title: Order of execution in an IF/ELIF/ELSE chain
data.instruction: Put the steps in the correct order showing how Python processes an IF/ELIF/ELSE structure.
items: Evaluate the IF condition — is it True or False?
If the IF condition is True, execute the IF block and skip all remaining ELIF and ELSE blocks
If the IF condition is False, move to the first ELIF and evaluate its condition
If the ELIF condition is True, execute that ELIF block and skip remaining branches
If all IF and ELIF conditions are False, execute the ELSE block
Continue with the code after the entire IF/ELIF/ELSE structure

data.title: Steps to trace a selection program for a given input
data.instruction: Put these tracing steps in the correct order.
items: Note the input value that will be used
Evaluate the IF condition using the input value and determine if it is True or False
If True, identify which block will execute; if False, move to the next condition
Continue evaluating ELIF conditions in order until a True one is found
If no condition is True, identify that the ELSE block will execute
Record the output that the chosen block produces
